_help.about: Design §CV (wired by Claude Code, 3 Oct: Smoke, shaders/smoke.gdshader, Campfire, OldHearths, NestBuilder; the swifts' chatter and the stack mouth's sparks at night are not built yet). Smoke (Mike, 3 Oct): every lit hearth sends up a column you can read from far off; the ruins' underground hearths breathe through a stack above each one; a cold stack is a place swifts roost; a wildfire has its own plume. Every number is a first guess; the designer owns them and the eye is Claude Code's. tools/smoke_check.py is the gate (0 errors before commit). Restart after editing.
_help.hearth: The column over a lit fire. sources: which fires smoke (a camp's hearth, a rekindled old hearth, a nest's hearth, a delve's hearths through their stacks). never: lights that never smoke (emptied by Mike, 3 Oct: "all fire should smoke based off flame size"; torches, lamps and the pipe's brand joined sources). by_flame: a fire smokes by its flame's size against a campfire's (1.0): its column is the by_state row x size^exponent (2: the fire's heat goes with its flame's area), so the torch's burnt end (an ember, the embers row, at look.json fire.flame.torch.scale 0.32) sends up a wisp under a metre, a tomb lamp (0.14) a thread a little over a metre, a campfire its full column; the fire lights sqrt of that scale as much of it at night (wired by Claude Code, 3 Oct). by_state: one row per FireStore state (flames, flare, low, embers, out): top_m is how high the column stands in still air, width_m its width at the base, density how solid it draws (0-1). The embers row is the thin wisp that says a fire can still be saved (§BL). stack_scale: a column leaving a stack is this share of an open fire's. rise_mps: how fast the noise scrolls up. wind: the column leans lean_deg_per_mps degrees from upright for each m/s of the weather sim's wind at that place, up to max_lean_deg, and leans more toward its top (shear); below calm_below_mps it stands straight. calm_pool: in still air around dawn the smoke stops rising at at_m and spreads spread_m flat over the valley. rain: above from_mm_h the column is top_scale as tall and density_scale as solid. night: the column is not drawn (smoke gives off no light); the fire lights the first fire_lit_m of it warm and the canopy above (§BZ). look: the same family as §BZ's flame: `cards` camera-facing cards, noise scrolled upward and posterised to `bands` flat bands on a `texels` grid, nearest-filtered, cut out by dither (no soft alpha). colour_near / colour_far: pale blue-grey, never neutral grey (LOOK_REFERENCE R3), lighter and bluer with distance; colour_shade is its own shaded side. far: a camp that is not loaded still has a fire state in the sim (§BL), so its column is drawn from that number out to seen_to_m; min_px is the narrowest it may draw.
_help.outlets: Where a hearth's smoke leaves (Mike: primitive camps on the surface need nothing; a cave mouth clears itself; in ruins a chimney above each hearth). open: places whose fire is open to the sky. mouth: nests (landforms.json ids) whose hearth sits under rock: the smoke clears through the mouth and up the cliff, and the soot above the mouth stays when the fire is out. by_ruin: the stack above a delve's hearths, by ruin kind (the same keys as delves.json fire_holders.by_ruin). surface_old_hearth: a ruin's surface old hearth (OldHearths): a fireplace under a standing stack in a castle or tower, the open ring elsewhere. per_delve: own_stack lists the hearths that get their own flue and stack; share_nearest lists the fire-holders that vent through the nearest one. forms: each stack's shape: height_m above the ground or roof [min, max], width_m, at (where on the ruin when it is not free-standing), open_front (a fireplace you can still swing a torch into, §CN), soot_lip (black round the mouth so it reads as a chimney). soot: its colour (navy-black, never grey) and how far the streak runs. passable: a flue is never a way in or out (§CJ.4 unchanged). night_mouth: a lit hearth below shows as a faint glow and a few sparks at the stack's mouth.
_help.swifts: Chimney swifts take the cold stacks (Mike). cold_game_days: how long the hearth below must have been out. share_of_stacks: the share of suitable cold stacks that hold a flock. flock: birds per stack [min, max]. forms: which stack forms are wide enough. min_width_m: the narrowest mouth they use. climate: where they live (annual mean temperature in C, moisture 0-1); first guess until each land gets its own swift by realm (§AA, §CS). day_range_m: how far from the stack they hunt by day. dusk: the flock circles over the stack for circle_game_min, then pours in over enter_game_min while the sun is between sun_deg[0] and sun_deg[1] degrees (part of §CH's handover). dawn: they pour out over leave_game_min. sound: their chatter, a point source at the stack (§BG). lit_below: light the hearth and they leave at once, stay away while it is in any of stay_away_states, and return after it has been cold return_after_cold_game_days. overrun.roost: false means no swifts over an overrun delve (§CN: the place goes quiet), so a cold stack with no birds at dusk is a far-off hint; a first guess for the designer to confirm. species: the real bird and its sources. later: where this goes next.
_help.wildfire_plume: A wildfire's own smoke (proposed in chat on 3 Oct, not objected to; the designer can strike it): wide, tall and dark so it is never mistaken for a hearth's narrow pale column. top_m, width_m: its size at full burn. lean_deg_per_mps: its lean with the wind. colours: dark indigo, never grey. night_base_glow: the fire lights its base orange at night. seen_to_m: how far off it draws. §BL's wildfire rules are unchanged.

outlets._help_do_ds: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DR, §DS; crag_fortress is wired, §DO, temple_city, §DR (a vent shaft over its delve hearths, on the sanctum's roof), long_wall, §DS.1 (a wall flue over its gate tower's delve hearths), carved_cliffs, §DS.2 (open_ring: no stack, the soot carved over the facade doors), cliff_dwelling, §DS.4 (roof_vent over its delve hearths), brick_city, §DS.6 (roof_vent over the vaults' hearths), stone_heads, §DS.3 (open_ring: no built hearth, the quarry's hearth rings only), terraced_pueblo, §DS.5 (roof_vent over its delve hearths), and stone_circle, §DS.7 (none: its souterrain has no fire-holders): its delve hearths stack on the roof above them, OldHearths] New kinds: crag_fortress vents each delve hearth through a roof vent (the honest form is the rooftop burner those buildings had); temple_city vents through the towers (vent_shaft); long_wall through its towers' wall flues; carved_cliffs out the facade doors with soot above them (open_ring stands in: no stack); stone_heads and stone_circle have no built hearth (open); terraced_pueblo out the roof hatches (roof_vent); tower_house the castle's chimney stack; the broch a central hearth under an open roof.
outlets._help_dt_dz: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DT–§DZ] hanging_gardens: the gallery hearths vent through the terraces' drains (vent_shaft stands in); abbey: the warming house's chimney stack; colonnade, temple_park, pillar_shrines and hewn_temple have no stack (open fires only, or none).

species.name: Chimney swift
species.source: All About Birds, Chimney Swift, Life History (allaboutbirds.org/guide/Chimney_Swift/lifehistory): nests and roosts in chimneys, air vents, old wells and abandoned cisterns; before chimneys, in caves and the hollow trees of old-growth forest; the nest is a half-saucer of twigs cemented to the wall with saliva; it cannot perch and clings to vertical walls; at dusk flocks funnel into a roosting chimney, up to 10,000 on migration; eats flying insects; breeds in eastern North America and winters in the upper Amazon basin. Wikipedia, Vaux's swift: the western relative does the same in hollow trees and chimneys, entering in roughly 30 minutes between sunset and dark.
